McLaren: McLaren has reshaped the diffuser at the car’s rear, smoothing the airflow underneath to generate extra down‑force and give the car tighter grip in the high‑speed corners. They’ve also added a new winglet on the rear‑brake duct, which channels air more efficiently, improving rear‑end stability and shaving a bit of drag on the straights. Together, these tweaks should help the team extract more pace and confidence throughout this weekend’s lap‑times.
Scuderia Ferrari: Ferrari has trimmed and reshaped the top flap of its rear wing and lightened both that wing and the lower “beam” wing, shaving off a bit of drag. The sleeker rear end should give the car higher straight‑line speed while still keeping enough downforce to stay planted through the corners. In short, the car will be quicker on the straights without sacrificing the grip needed for the race.
Red Bull Racing: Red Bull has opened up the centre of the engine cover, giving the car a bigger “exit” that helps keep temperatures in check and reduces the chance of a reliability hiccup over the weekend. They’ve also trimmed and flattened the lower beam‑wing – a subtle reshape that eases the load on the front of the car, sharpening its front‑end grip and making the car feel more stable through the corners. Together, these tweaks aim to keep the RB stable and fast, especially in the high‑downforce sections of the circuit.
Mercedes F1 Team: Mercedes F1 Team did not submit any updates for this event.
Aston Martin: Aston Martin has swapped to a milder rear‑wing flap for this circuit, dialing back the aggressive angle to cut drag. The change lets the car carry more straight‑line speed and stay gentler on the tyres, giving the team a better balance between corner grip and pace on the long straights this weekend. In short, it’s a simple tweak that could translate into a stronger fight for points on race day.
Alpine F1 Team: Alpine F1 Team did not submit any updates for this event.
Haas F1 Team: Haas has tweaked its aero package for the weekend: the rear wing is now set to a lower‑drag, decambered configuration, and the front wing’s flaps have been relaxed to match. These changes reduce overall drag, giving the car a higher top‑speed on the straights while still keeping enough balance for the corners, which should help Haas be more competitive on this circuit’s mix of fast sections and medium‑speed turns.
Racing Bulls / RB: Racing Bulls has trimmed the front‑wing flaps and toned down the rear‑wing angles, while also slimming the lower beam‑wing element. These changes lower overall drag, giving the car better straight‑line speed on this circuit’s long laps without sacrificing the balance needed through the corners. In short, the car should be quicker on the straights and more stable through the turns, a crucial edge for this weekend’s race.

Sauber / Audi: Sauber‑Audi has fitted a low‑balance front‑wing flap and a reshaped central floor to smooth out airflow, plus a brand‑new beam wing and rear‑wing endplates that cut drag. The rear wing itself has also been re‑profiled for a lower‑drag setup, giving the car more straight‑line speed without sacrificing too much down‑force. In short, the aero tweaks should make the car quicker on the straights and more stable through the corners at this weekend’s circuit.
